input.customer_message: Small bug: If you connect to a wireless display in Win 10, and then you reposition or resize the display, you introduce lag. @MicrosoftHelps
input.conversation_context:
MICROSOFT (1582400): @487068 Thanks for reaching out. Just to clarify, have you tried connecting a different wireless display to see if same issue persists?
CUSTOMER (1582401): @MicrosoftHelps No. I don't have another to test with. That would be a good test though.
CUSTOMER (1582402): @MicrosoftHelps I've been able to reproduce reliably. Work-around is to disconnect and reconnect again.
CUSTOMER (1582403): @MicrosoftHelps The more times I applied changes, the more lag I experienced. It seems like a memory leak.
MICROSOFT (1582404): @487068 Let's see if performing a clean boot will do the trick: https://t.co/HgI0ZpCFMM. Let us know how it goes.
CUSTOMER (1582405): @MicrosoftHelps 1) clean booted. msconfig disable all. taskman disable all. restart. wait for caching.
2) conn to wi-dev
3 test 4 move/resize disp. 5 test
CUSTOMER (1582406): @MicrosoftHelps so... the lag is not present. clearly it's a 3rd party driver problem (as in: not yours!) -- thank you for the troubleshooting help!
MICROSOFT (1582407): @487068 2/2 Also, help us improve our social media support by answering a quick survey. Rate us here: https://t.co/spiPdS9LU9.
MICROSOFT (1582408): @487068 ½ Glad to know that we were able to determine the cause of it. You know we're just a tweet away if you have other queries.
CUSTOMER (1582409): @MicrosoftHelps Done. Thanks.
input.generated_reply: We are sorry to hear you are experiencing lag when repositioning or resizing a wireless display in Windows 10. Since we do not have specific troubleshooting steps for this in our current records, please contact Microsoft support directly for further assistance.
